title: Collect every VCF Operations for Logs agent group in stable order
prompt:
Complete `VcfOpsLogAgentGroups/VcfOpsLogAgentGroups.psm1` as a PowerShell 7.4 module that retrieves the complete VCF Operations for Logs agent-group collection and emits it in deterministic order.

Read the protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. The focused REST contract was projected directly from `specifications/vcf-operations/log-management-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the immutable VCF 9.1 release commit recorded in both files. The JSON specification, not a rendered documentation page, is authoritative. Use exactly the operationId `getAllAgentGroupConfig`.

VCF PowerCLI 9.1 supplies `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` version `13.5.0.25380678` as an environment prerequisite. Keep that genuine external module prerequisite in the protected manifest. Do not install, download, copy, generate, vendor, intercept, redefine, replace, or imitate VMware modules, SDK assemblies, specifications, or harness tools. This module is a focused log-management REST extension to the authenticated VCF Operations workflow: the caller supplies the Log Management origin and the `X-JWT-Token` obtained for service key `ops-li`. Use `System.Net.Http.HttpClient`; do not use `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, curl, a subprocess, or raw sockets.

Preserve and export only:

`Get-VcfOpsLogAgentGroupInventory -BaseUri <uri> -LogToken <string> [-PageSize <1..1000>] [-HttpClient <System.Net.Http.HttpClient>]`

`PageSize` defaults to 100. `BaseUri` must be an absolute HTTP(S) origin with no credentials, query, fragment, or non-root path. Reject a blank or CR/LF-containing token before traffic. When `HttpClient` is omitted, create one that does not follow redirects and dispose only the client and handler that the function owns. A supplied client is caller-owned.

Invoke `getAllAgentGroupConfig` for every page. Page zero is exactly a bodyless `GET /api/v2/agent/groups?page=0&size=<PageSize>`; subsequent targets increment `page` by one. The OpenAPI `pageable` query object uses the query parameter defaults `style=form` and `explode=true`, so the selected `page` and `size` members appear as those two query pairs in that exact order. The optional `sort` member is unset: omit it entirely rather than sending an empty value, JSON, null, or a default. Never append a bare `?`. Every request has exactly one `Accept: application/json` and one `X-JWT-Token`, and has no request body or Content-Type. Require exactly HTTP 200.

The specification models the success body as an array of `Page` objects whose `content` items are objects. The focused scenario returns exactly one `Page` object per request, with `number`, `size`, `numberOfElements`, `totalElements`, `totalPages`, `first`, `last`, `empty`, and `content`. Validate those fields, require the page number requested, require internally consistent and invariant totals, and continue until `last` is true. Reject a non-progressing/repeated page, inconsistent metadata, duplicate nonblank ordinal `id` values across pages, malformed group data, early `last`, or a final item count different from `totalElements`. Buffer the whole collection before writing any success output, so a later-page failure returns no partial inventory.

For this focused projection, each `content` item follows the protected contract's `AgentGroupResponse` profile. Require nonblank string `id` and `name`, Boolean `autoUpdate`, and an `info` value that is either a string or null. Project each item to exactly these properties in order: `Id`, `Name`, `AutoUpdate`, `Info`. Emit the complete collection sorted by `Name`, then `Id`, using ordinal, case-sensitive comparison. Page boundaries and server item order are not output order. Write no progress or diagnostics to the success pipeline. Errors must not expose the log token, response bodies, or nested transport messages.

Run `python3 -B .protected/verify.py`. The protected verifier starts a contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port, generates the token and every agent-group identity at runtime, and reads its flushed and fsynced JSONL request log. The mock derives its complete method/path allow-list from `docs/contract.json`, serves only the named operation, returns three pages per invocation, and changes page composition and item order while keeping collection membership fixed. Verification asserts complete retrieval, stable ordinal ordering, exact ordered methods and raw targets, header multiplicity, zero-byte bodies, omission of `sort` and every empty optional value, no extra calls, and no credential leakage. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

Everything under `.protected/` and `docs/`, plus `VcfOpsLogAgentGroups/VcfOpsLogAgentGroups.psd1`, is protected. Edit only `VcfOpsLogAgentGroups/VcfOpsLogAgentGroups.psm1`.
scenario: the agent-group collection spans three pages whose composition and item order change between otherwise identical inventory calls
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback request log proves complete zero-based pagination and total omission of the unset Pageable.sort member
